newsitem.title: FRANCE: France hints at possible contacts with Kabila.
newsitem.headline: France hints at possible contacts with Kabila.

text.p: France, a longtime backer of Zaire's embattled President Mobutu Sese Seko, hinted on Monday it may be talking with his rebel foe Laurent Kabila as part of efforts to secure a settlement.

"We are not ruling out any party in our contacts to help solve the crisis," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told reporters when asked whether Paris was making contact with the rebels who have vowed to unseat Mobutu.
Pressed to say whether contacts had already taken place, Rummelhardt gave the same answer.

As Kabila's forces advanced through Zaire, Paris, which has backed Mobutu during most of his 32-year autocratic rule, recently began distancing itself from him while calling on the rebels to seek a peaceful settlement rather than carry out their threat to take Kinshasa.
Rebels now hold about half the sprawling country and Kabila has suggested he is ready to force Mobutu out in a final advance on the capital, the last stronghold of Zaire's ragged army.
Rummelhardt said France was backing efforts by South African President Nelson Mandela and U.N. special envoy Mohammed Sahnoun to secure talks between Mobutu and Kabila.
He said France wanted talks to establish a mechanism to start a transition towards democracy.
"It is inadmissible to prolong and worsen the plight of civilians," Rummelhardt said. France has said the rebels could be responsible for a humanitarian disaster if they kept on fighting.
